subject.title: gateway install/status hardcodes ~/Library/LaunchAgents — prevents boot-without-login on macOS

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class macOS system LaunchDaemon gateway mode, and what sudo, UserName, environment, status, and lifecycle contract should that mode use?
rationale: Automation should not choose this boundary because it controls privileged launchd mutation, execution user identity, boot-before-login behavior, service environment durability, and coexistence with existing user LaunchAgents.

options.title: Add audited system scope
options.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add an explicit system LaunchDaemon mode or scope, and align install/status/lifecycle/doctor/docs/tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep diagnostic guidance only
options.body: Do not manage LaunchDaemons yet; improve status/doctor/docs so operators can inspect and repair custom LaunchDaemons manually.

options.title: Defer LaunchDaemon support
options.body: Leave boot-without-login unsupported until companion-app or installer ownership is ready to own the privileged service UX.

recommendation.title: Add audited system scope
recommendation.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as the default, add an explicit system LaunchDaemon mode or scope, and align install/status/lifecycle/doctor/docs/tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available history on the gateway lifecycle adapter and prior reviews route the launchd scope decision there.
